places.name: Big Bend Ranch State Park
places.coord_point: Barton Warnock Visitor Center, east entrance, 21800 FM 170, Terlingua
nearby: Presidio (nearest town, Wikipedia; no distance stated)
Lajitas (Wikipedia lead says the park HQ is there; no distance stated)
places.blurb: Texas's biggest state park on the Rio Grande, with primitive and equestrian campsites and an International Dark Sky Park.
places.status_note: TPWD page shows active alerts (a screwworm alert link; alert text not read). Reservations highly recommended because the park often reaches capacity.
places.notes: NAME CANDIDATES (ten): Azimuth, Gazetteer, Theodolite, Chainline, Transit-Glass, Plotter, Survey-Staff, Bearing-Pin, Declinator, Lodestar. Chosen: Lodestar. POINT: the TPWD east-entrance point (Barton Warnock Visitor Center). The Wikipedia infobox point 29.53056, -104.15444 is a park-centre point about 48 km away, so it is not used. Wikipedia's lead places the HQ at Lajitas while the TPWD address is Terlingua; TPWD used. COUNTY: Wikipedia says Brewster and Presidio; the point is in Brewster. ACREAGE: 311,000 from the Wikipedia infobox (TPWD prints no figure). CAMPING: TPWD lists 'drive-up or hike-in primitive sites' and 'equestrian sites'. Backcountry is referred to but not described. The Sauceda Bunkhouse is lodging listed apart. Tent, RV, cabin, group and dispersed are not stated. RESERVATIONS: the general reservation site is used; district pages are Interior (texasstateparks.reserveamerica.com/big-bend-ranch-state-park/r/facilityDetails.do) and River (texasstateparks.reserveamerica.com/camping/barton-warnock-visitor-center/r/facilityDetails.do). Phone (512) 389-8900. ACCESS: TPWD's Fort Leaton page says motor homes and trailers are not recommended on the 27-mile road to the interior Sauceda Ranger Station. DARK SKY: darksky.org returned HTTP 403 to my fetches, so the 2017 year comes from a search summary of the darksky.org listing and DarkSky's November 21, 2017 news release (darksky.org/news/big-bend-ranch-state-park-named-worlds-newest-international-dark-sky-park/). TPWD also says the park 'has been designated an International Dark Sky Park'. A Greater Big Bend International Dark Sky Reserve (certified 2022, search summary) also covers the park: darksky.org/places/greater-big-bend-international-dark-sky-reserve/.

places.name: Cooper State Park
places.coord_point: park headquarters per TPWD, South Sulphur Unit, 1690 FM 3505, Sulphur Springs
nearby: Cooper (Doctors Creek Unit address; Wikipedia's nearest city)
Jim Chapman Lake (the lake the park sits on, per Wikipedia)
places.blurb: Two units on Jim Chapman Lake: Doctors Creek and South Sulphur, with cabins, screened shelters and horse camps.
places.status_note: TPWD page shows active alerts (alert text not read). Equestrian trails may close in wet weather.
places.notes: NAME: the TPWD page reads 'Cooper State Park'; Wikipedia says it was previously 'Cooper Lake State Park'. POINT: TPWD names the South Sulphur Unit as park headquarters. The Doctors Creek Unit point (95 Park Road 8154, Cooper; 33.348700, -95.663677) is about 6.8 km north. COUNTY: Wikipedia assigns South Sulphur to Hopkins and Doctors Creek to Delta; the point is in Hopkins. ACREAGE: 3,026 acres from Wikipedia (TPWD gives only a trail figure of nearly 600 acres). CAMPING: 'sites with water and electricity' coded rv_hookups; screened shelters, cabins with kitchens and bathrooms (South Sulphur), equestrian, and group sites from the menu labels. 'Walk-in campsite' is listed but not classified, and tent camping is not stated, so neither is coded. PHONES: Doctors Creek (903) 395-3100; South Sulphur (903) 945-5256; state line (512) 389-8900. DARK SKY: the DarkSky search returned no Cooper listing, so dark_sky is null; this is not confirmed as absent.

places.name: Fort Leaton State Historic Site
places.coord_point: park address point, 16952 FM 170 East, Presidio (TPWD does not label it HQ or entrance)
nearby: Big Bend Ranch State Park (TPWD calls this site its west entrance)
places.blurb: A historic fort that is day-use only, and the west gate into Big Bend Ranch State Park.
places.status_note: Day-use site: open daily except Christmas Day, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (TPWD). TPWD page shows active alerts (alert text not read).
places.notes: CAMPING: no camping at the fort itself (TPWD: 'The fort is a day-use site'), so camping is false. The primitive drive-in and hike-in campsites belong to Big Bend Ranch State Park and are reached through this west entrance; their reservations are on the Big Bend Ranch pages. ACREAGE: Wikipedia infobox says 23.4 acres and its lead says 23.5; 23.4 used. COORDINATES: the TPWD point agrees with the Wikipedia infobox point 29.54250, -104.32639 to within a few metres. PHONE: (512) 389-8900.

places.name: Hueco Tanks State Park & Historic Site
places.coord_point: park GPS point per TPWD (the page warns GPS may misdirect; street address 6900 Hueco Tanks Road No. 1, El Paso)
nearby: El Paso (about 32 mi northeast of the city centre, Wikipedia)
Franklin Mountains (west of the park, Wikipedia; no distance stated)
Hueco Mountains (east of the park, Wikipedia; no distance stated)
places.blurb: A mainly day-use desert park near El Paso, where North Mountain access is capped at 70 people a day by permit.
places.status_note: Mainly a day-use park. Access is restricted to protect fragile resources, and special reservation and entry restrictions are in place. TPWD page shows active alerts (alert text not read).
places.notes: CAMPING: TPWD says the park has '20 campsites' but does not list their types, so camping_kinds is null. CONTACTS: reserve by phone (512) 389-8911; guided tours (915) 857-1135, booked at least one week ahead. COORDINATES: the Wikipedia infobox point 31.92028, -106.03861 is about 0.8 km from the TPWD point, within the 2 km tolerance; TPWD used. ACREAGE: 860 acres (350 ha) from Wikipedia. COUNTY: El Paso from Wikipedia; TPWD prints no county. TYPE: the official name is 'State Park & Historic Site'; 'State Park' is used. The 70-person North Mountain permit figure is from TPWD.

places.name: Lake Somerville State Park & Trailway
places.coord_point: Birch Creek Unit, 14222 Park Road 57, Somerville (TPWD does not say which unit is headquarters)
nearby: Burton (nearest town per Wikipedia; no distance stated)
Nails Creek Unit (the park's second unit, Ledbetter address)
places.blurb: Two units, Birch Creek and Nails Creek, with water and electric sites, Trailway primitive camps and horse sites.
places.status_note: TPWD page shows active alerts (alert text not read). Reservations recommended for camping and day use.
places.notes: COUNTY: Wikipedia's lead says the park lies in Lee and Burleson counties without assigning each unit. The county 'Burleson' for the Birch Creek point is NOT GIS-verified. POINT CHOICE: Birch Creek is used because it carries the Somerville address; TPWD does not name the HQ unit. NAILS CREEK POINT (TPWD): 30.290719, -96.667214 at 6280 FM 180, Ledbetter; the Wikipedia infobox point 30.29083, -96.66722 matches that Nails Creek point. ACREAGE: 8,700 acres from the Wikipedia infobox; TPWD's 11,000+ acres is lake water, not park land. CAMPING: 'sites with water and electricity' coded rv_hookups; 'primitive sites along the Trailway' coded primitive; 'equestrian campsites' and 'Horse Sites' coded equestrian; the 'Group Sites' menu label coded group. Tent and cabins are not stated. PHONES: Birch Creek (979) 535-7763; Nails Creek (979) 289-2392. DARK SKY: the DarkSky search returned no listing, so dark_sky is null; this is not confirmed as absent.

places.name: Monahans Sandhills State Park
places.coord_point: TPWD point at the park address, 101 Park Road 41, Monahans (TPWD does not label it HQ or entrance)
nearby: Monahans (nearest town, Wikipedia; no distance stated)
Llano Estacado (region named in the Wikipedia lead; no distance stated)
places.blurb: A sandhills park near Monahans with 25 water-and-electric campsites and an 800-acre equestrian area.
places.status_note: TPWD page shows active alerts (alert text not read). The park often reaches capacity, so reservations are recommended.
places.notes: COORDINATE DISAGREEMENT: the Wikipedia infobox point 31.64750, -102.82306 is about 3.4 km from the TPWD point, which is over the 2 km tolerance. The TPWD point is used as the official one. COUNTY: Wikipedia lists Ward and Winkler counties; TPWD prints none. 'Ward' is NOT GIS-verified against the point. ACREAGE: 3,840 acres from Wikipedia; TPWD gives only the 800-acre equestrian area. CAMPING: '25 campsites with water and electricity' coded rv_hookups; 'three campsites' in the equestrian area coded equestrian. The group hall and pavilion are rentals, not camping, so group is not listed. Tent, primitive and cabins are not stated. PHONE: (512) 389-8900.

places.name: Ray Roberts Lake State Park
places.coord_point: Isle du Bois Unit, 100 PW 4137, Pilot Point (neither source says which unit is headquarters)
nearby: Pilot Point (nearest town, Wikipedia; no distance stated)
Lake Ray Roberts (29,000-acre lake, per TPWD)
places.blurb: Three developed units near the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex on a 29,000-acre lake, with horse sites, group camps and Lone Star Lodge.
places.status_note: TPWD page shows active alerts (alert text not read). Emerald ash borer quarantine: buy firewood where you plan to burn it (TPWD).
places.notes: CAMPING: 'Campsites' (type not stated) are not classified, so camping_kinds is partial. 'Horse Sites' coded equestrian; 'group walk-in campsites' coded group; Lone Star Lodge and Marina rooms coded lodge ((940) 686-0261, lonestar-lodge.com). HQ: neither source names one. COUNTY: Wikipedia places the whole park in Denton County. The Johnson Branch Unit (100 PW 4153, Valley View, 33.429802, -97.056449) was not checked separately for county. ACREAGE: 3,777 acres from Wikipedia; TPWD gives only the 29,000-acre lake. COORDINATES: the Isle du Bois point agrees with the Wikipedia infobox point 33.36556, -97.01194 to about 15 m. PHONE: (512) 389-8900. DARK SKY: none found in the DarkSky search.

places.name: Big Bend National Park
places.coord_point: PARK-LEVEL POINT, NOT THE HQ: Wikipedia infobox centre point. The NPS pages print no coordinates for the Panther Junction Visitor Center or park HQ.
nearby: Cañón de Santa Elena (adjoins the park in Mexico, per Wikipedia)
Maderas del Carmen (adjoins the park in Mexico, per Wikipedia)
Study Butte (access town; NPS directions put park HQ 26 miles east of it)
places.blurb: Chisos Mountains, desert and the Rio Grande, with developed campgrounds, a concession RV park and Chisos Mountains Lodge.
places.status_note: Cottonwood Campground is closed for summer. Chisos Basin and Rio Grande Village campgrounds require reservations (NPS camping page, last updated July 20, 2026).
places.notes: COORDINATES: no visitor-center or HQ coordinates are printed on the NPS planyourvisit or directions pages. The lat/lon is the Wikipedia infobox park centre (29.25000, -103.25000) and is NOT a visitor centre. Replace it with the Panther Junction point when one is found. HQ: Panther Junction Visitor Center at park headquarters, PO Box 129, Big Bend National Park, TX 79834-0129; phone 432-477-2251. Directions: 26 miles east of Study Butte, via TX 118 from Alpine or FM 170 from Presidio. CAMPING (NPS camping page, updated July 20, 2026): Chisos Basin Campground open, reservations required; Rio Grande Village Campground open, reservations required; Cottonwood Campground closed for summer; Rio Grande Village RV Park (concession operated by Aramark, 855-765-1324) with '25 sites with full hook-ups' coded rv_hookups. The NPS campground descriptions give no tent, cabin or group types, so tent is not coded. Primitive and backcountry come from the separate section on the same page. Chisos Mountains Lodge, 'the only lodging within Big Bend National Park', is coded lodge. reservations_url is null because no reservation link is printed on the NPS pages. DARK SKY: the darksky.org place page returned HTTP 403 to my fetches. A search summary gave 2012 (one IDA page, also Wikipedia's body) and 2014 (an IDA addendum), so year is null. A Greater Big Bend International Dark Sky Reserve (certified 2022, search summary) also covers the area. ACREAGE: 801,163 from the Wikipedia infobox.

places.name: Waco Mammoth National Monument
places.coord_point: monument site point from the Wikipedia infobox (the NPS page prints no coordinates); the Welcome Center is at 6220 Steinbeck Bend Drive, Waco, TX 76708
places.blurb: Waco's mammoth site, with guided tours from the Welcome Center that need no reservation.
places.status_note: Guided tours need no reservation (NPS). School field trips: 254-686-0168, or the NPS online sign-up.
places.notes: CAMPING: the NPS planyourvisit page does not state camping either way, and camping.htm returned HTTP 404. Camping is null, not false; verify on the NPS site. COORDINATES: the NPS page prints none; the Wikipedia infobox point is used and is not confirmed against the Welcome Center address. COUNTY: McLennan comes from Wikipedia's category tags, not its infobox. Waco as McLennan's county seat is from general knowledge, not from a fetched page, and is flagged for checking. ACREAGE: 5 acres (about 2.0 ha) from the Wikipedia infobox. NEARBY: only the nearest city is sourced; no other place with a distance was found, so the list is short. DARK SKY: not searched; no listing found.
